name: Sengmai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Devi, Ch. Chandrakala. 1993. A comparative study of Imphal, Sekmai and Khurkhul dialects of Meiteirol. PhD thesis, Manipur University (Shodhganga 10603/105254).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Sengmai proper: describes the Meitei (mani1292) dialect now spoken at Sekmai. scanned contents: Ch. I 'Inventory of phonemes' has 1.1.3 Toneme and 1.1.4 Juncture, no stress/accent section; Ch. II phonological correspondences incl. 2.3 tonal correspondences. Chapter I (phonemes) not downloaded/scanned; intro and ch. 2 are scans without text layer, not scanned.

sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke. 2020. On the genetic position of Chakpa within Luish languages. Himalayan Linguistics 19(2): 44–55. doi:10.5070/H91150999
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.2.4 Tones, p. 49: 'Generally speaking, tones of Chakpa are unknown as they are no longer spoken nor recorded. Ch. Y. Singh (2014) shows two distinctive tones (mid and high) for Chakpa [Andro]. However, compared with Cak, Kadu, and Ganan, the correspondence is irregular.' Sec. 1 p. 45 identifies McCulloch 1859 as 'the best material published so far' on Chakpa (Andro and Sengmai), plus Basanta 2008: 194–199 (100 words) and Rorendrajit 2006 (Sekmai sample).

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2013. Re-examining the genetic position of Jingpho: putting flesh on the bones of the Jingpho/Luish relationship. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 36(2): 15–95. doi:10.32655/ltba.36.2.02
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Sengmai stress or tone. Sec. 4 p. ~38 notes Andro, Sengmai and Chairel 'have all gone extinct' (fn. 21) and are known from McCulloch 1859; Andro/Sengmai forms cited only as untoned romanized cognates (A/Se) in comparative tables; tone discussion is about Kadu, Sak, Jingpho, Lahu.

sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke (藤原敬介). 2012. ルイ祖語の再構にむけて (Toward a reconstruction of Proto-Luish). 京都大学言語学研究 (Kyoto University Linguistic Research) 31: 25–131. doi:10.14989/182194
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Data-sources note p. 31: Andro (A) and Sengmai (Se) are taken from McCulloch 1859 and '声調は記録されていない' (tones are not recorded); Proto-Luish reconstructed with two tones H/L (sec. 6, p. 117) from Cak/Kadu/Ganan only.

sources.citation: Hodson, T. C. 1908. The Meitheis. London: David Nutt.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnography only; mentions the Lois of Sengmai (Sekmai), Andro and Chairel as villages/tribes (pp. 9, 15 etc.); no Sengmai vocabulary or phonology.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.), Konow, S. 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Part III (Tibeto-Burman family: Kuki-Chin and Burma groups), 'Loi' section p. 43 and 'Standard words and sentences in Meithei, Andro, Sengmai, and Chairel' (McCulloch's data reprinted).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States 'None of these dialects has been returned for the survey, and they have probably all disappeared'; reprints McCulloch's vocabulary as an appendix to Meithei; no grammatical or phonological description.

sources.citation: McCulloch, W. 1859. Account of the Valley of Munnipore and of the Hill Tribes; with a Comparative Vocabulary of the Munnipore and other Languages. Selections from the Records of the Government of India (Foreign Department) No. XXVII. Calcutta. Appendix: comparative vocabulary, 'Undro and Sengmai' column.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary record of the language: a ~420-item comparative wordlist with a few sentences, Andro and Sengmai in one shared column; preface gives only a vowel/consonant pronunciation key (a as in Italian, oo, th aspirated, gh) and no accent marks or stress remarks ('the ear is deceptive').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page, Sengmai [seng1275] (Hammarström et al.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Zero descriptive references; note says the language is 'documented by a wordlist in McCulloch, W. 1859' and is extinct (Moseley 2010); subclassification refs DeLancey 2015, van Driem 2001, Matisoff 2012, Huziwara 2019/2020.
Nothing; used only to locate the Huziwara 2012/2020, Matisoff 2013 and Basanta 2008 citations. Wikidata lists glottocodes seng1274 and seng1275 for the same item.

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 Huziwara, Keisuke. 2013b. アンドロ語文法の再構 (A reconstruction of Andro grammar). 日本歴史言語学会第3回大会 (Japanese Society for Historical Linguistics, 3rd meeting), talk.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Re-examines all Chakpa (Andro/Sengmai) data in McCulloch 1859 and Basanta 2008 and reconstructs the grammar; the closest thing to a grammatical description of the language. Not found online.

sources.citation: Singh, Ch. Yashawanta. 2014. A linguistic study of dead language — Chakpa. Paper presented at SEALS 24, Yangon University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only fieldwork-based account of Chakpa (Andro variety) with ritual-language speakers; Huziwara 2020: 49 reports it gives two tones (mid, high); might also comment on accent. Unpublished conference paper.

sources.citation: Basanta, Ningombam. 2008. Modernisation, Challenge and Response: A Study of the Chakpa Community of Manipur. New Delhi: Akansha Publishing House. (pp. 194–199: 100 basic words and sentences)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Second independent wordlist of Chakpa (community-collected, 20th/21st c.); could carry accent/tone marking that McCulloch lacks.

sources.citation: Rorendrajit, Kh. 2006. The Chakpa of Manipur: a brief historical account. Proceedings of North East India History Association 26: 299–313.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Contains a sample of Sekmai (Sengmai) basic words and sentences not in McCulloch (Huziwara 2020 fn. 4) — the only Sengmai-specific data besides 1859.

sources.citation: Damant, G. H. 1880. Notes on the locality and population of the tribes dwelling between the Brahmaputra and Ningthi rivers. Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society n.s. 12: 228–258 (Loi note pp. 241f; short Andro vocabulary p. 255).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second 19th-century primary record of the Loi languages (Andro list only); completeness of the primary-source base; unlikely to mention accent.
